Seamless 360 degree cylindrical panorama strip, a skybox backdrop for a stylised video game with the stylised realism of a modern arcade golf game: believable light and atmosphere, bold saturated colour, slightly painterly. A perfectly straight level horizon line runs across the whole image at one fifth of the height from the bottom edge. Below the horizon only black water mirroring city lights. Above it a night sky of deep indigo and violet with a few stars and thin clouds lit magenta from below, and a bright full moon in the left third two thirds of the way up the sky. All the way round the horizon stands an imaginary science-fiction city skyline in haze: hundreds of plain invented towers, every one a simple box, slab or cylinder with a perfectly flat level roof, of many heights and widths, with thousands of small lit windows, neon magenta and cyan edge lights, a few searchlight beams, the tallest towers reaching one third of the image height. Every roof is flat: no spires, no antennas, no masts, no needles, no pointed tops, no pyramid tops, no stepped or tiered crowns, no setbacks, no art deco towers, no domes, no arches, no clock towers, no pagodas, no twisted towers, no observation decks, no bridges, no wheels. Every building is a made-up generic shape: none may resemble any real-world building, tower or landmark, and the skyline must not resemble any real city. No signs, no lettering, no symbols, no hearts, no logos. No foreground objects, no people, no animals, no text, no lens flare streaks, no vignette, no frame. The left edge and the right edge match exactly so the strip wraps around seamlessly.
